bio: Dutch conductor and composer who served as first Kapellmeister of the Bavarian Radio Symphony Orchestra from 1950 to 1966 and later taught conducting at the Munich Hochschule. He wrote a substantial body of brass chamber and solo music, including trombone concertinos and several trombone quartets.

name: N. Rota
bio: Italian composer best known for his film scores for Federico Fellini and for The Godfather, alongside a large body of concert music. His 1966 Trombone Concerto has become a staple of the instrument’s solo repertoire.

name: Trummy Young
bio: American jazz trombonist who spent twelve years with Louis Armstrong's All Stars. He also worked with Jimmie Lunceford and Benny Goodman, and co-wrote "'Tain't What You Do (It's the Way That You Do It)".

name: S. Šulek
bio: Croatian composer, conductor, and violinist who taught composition at the Zagreb Academy of Music from 1948 to 1975. His Vox Gabrieli (1973) is a sonata for trombone and piano.

name: B. Harris
bio: American trombonist whose broad, vibrato-rich sound and rhythmic bite made him a star of Woody Herman's First Herd; he was also a member of Herman's Second Herd. He recorded widely with Herman and with Jazz at the Philharmonic, later worked in Las Vegas and retired to Florida.

name: H. Dutilleux
bio: French composer whose meticulously crafted works extended the legacies of Debussy and Ravel while developing a wholly individual voice. His Choral, Cadence et Fugato (1950) is for trombone and piano.

name: A. Arutiunian
bio: Armenian composer widely known for his Trumpet Concerto (1950). He headed the Armenian State Philharmonic from 1954 and served on the board of the Armenian Composers' Union; his brass works include a Trombone Concerto (1991) and a Tuba Concerto (1992), with Armenian folk music a strong influence.

name: K. Winding
bio: Danish-born American jazz trombonist best known for his partnership with J.J. Johnson in the Jay and Kai Quintet (1954-1956), and for playing on the Birth of the Cool sessions (1949). His version of More reached number eight on the Billboard Hot 100 in 1963.

name: K. Serocki
bio: Polish composer born in Toruń and co-founder of the Warsaw Autumn festival for contemporary music. He wrote the Concerto for Trombone and Orchestra (1953) and the Sonatina for Trombone and Piano (1954).

name: G. Walker
bio: American composer and pianist, the first African American to win the Pulitzer Prize for Music. He wrote five piano sonatas.

name: J.J. Johnson
bio: Widely regarded as the father of modern jazz trombone, Johnson was one of the earliest trombonists to embrace the fast, complex vocabulary of bebop. He worked with Charlie Parker, Dizzy Gillespie, and Miles Davis, and several of his compositions became jazz standards.

name: L. Berio
bio: Italian composer noted for his experimental work and his pioneering work in electronic music; in 1955 he co-founded the Studio di fonologia musicale in Milan with Bruno Maderna. His Sequenza V for solo trombone (1966), written for Stuart Dempster, calls for multiphonics and other extended techniques.

name: A. Grey
bio: American trombonist known as a master of the plunger mute and a member of the Count Basie Orchestra. He also played with Benny Carter, Lionel Hampton, and Dizzy Gillespie, and led his own groups into the 1990s.

name: M. Liston
bio: American jazz trombonist, composer, and arranger who was among the first women to achieve prominence as an instrumentalist in a male-dominated field. She formed a decades-long creative partnership with pianist Randy Weston and also wrote for Quincy Jones and Duke Ellington.

name: F. Rosolino
bio: American jazz trombonist from Detroit, one of the trombonists who developed the instrument to match the advances of bebop. He gained prominence with Gene Krupa's and Stan Kenton's bands and was active in Los Angeles recording studios in the 1960s and 1970s.

name: U. Green
bio: American jazz trombonist celebrated for his warm tone. He played in the big bands of Gene Krupa (from 1947) and Woody Herman, appeared on hundreds of recordings alongside artists such as Count Basie and Tony Bennett, and was inducted into the Alabama Jazz Hall of Fame in 1995.

name: J. Knepper
bio: American trombonist who worked with Stan Kenton, Benny Goodman, and the Thad Jones/Mel Lewis Orchestra.

name: F. Hidas
bio: Hungarian composer who served as music director of Budapest's National Theatre and later its Operetta Theatre before becoming a freelance composer. He became one of the foremost names in contemporary wind and brass repertoire, writing extensively for concert band and contributing concertos across the brass family, including for trombone.

name: G. Kurtág
bio: Hungarian composer and pianist whose interest in miniatures has often drawn comparisons to Webern. His Játékok ('Games') is an ongoing collection of piano pieces.

name: A. Mangelsdorff
bio: German jazz trombonist from Frankfurt who moved increasingly toward free jazz in the late 1960s and innovated multiphonics, enabling the trombone to sound multiple notes simultaneously. He helped rebuild Germany's post-war jazz scene, and his style and musical language are regarded as distinctive and independent of American models.

name: G. Roberts
bio: American bass trombonist nicknamed "Mr. Bass Trombone," a Los Angeles studio musician who played sessions with Frank Sinatra, Nelson Riddle, and Henry Mancini as well as on film scores including Jaws and Close Encounters of the Third Kind. Over a decades-long session career he played on more than 6,000 recordings and was one of the first bass trombonists to champion the instrument's solo possibilities.

name: C. Fontana
bio: American jazz trombonist regarded as the most fluid, innovative trombonist after J. J. Johnson. After working in the big bands of Woody Herman, Lionel Hampton, and Stan Kenton, he devoted most of his career to playing music in Las Vegas.

name: B. Brookmeyer
bio: American valve trombonist, pianist, and arranger who co-led a quintet with Clark Terry.

name: G. Crumb
bio: American avant-garde composer who won the 1968 Pulitzer Prize for Music and the 2001 Grammy Award for Best Contemporary Classical Composition. His four-volume piano set Makrokosmos (1972-1979) makes substantial use of inside-the-piano techniques.

name: D. Wick
bio: British trombonist who served as Principal Trombone of the London Symphony Orchestra from 1957 to 1988. He authored the textbook Trombone Technique and designed brass mouthpieces and mutes under the Denis Wick brand.

name: S. Gubaidulina
bio: Russian composer of Tatar heritage whose mystical music faced official condemnation in the Soviet Union. Her first major breakthrough was the violin concerto Offertorium (1980); her piano output includes the early Chaconne (1962) and Musical Toys (1968).

name: C. Fuller
bio: American jazz trombonist and pillar of the hard bop movement who recorded on John Coltrane's classic Blue Train and served as a member of Art Blakey's Jazz Messengers. Honored as an NEA Jazz Master in 2007.

name: Slide Hampton
bio: American jazz trombonist, composer, and arranger, known for his virtuosic playing and masterful arranging. One of the few left-handed trombonists, he won Grammy Awards in 1998 and 2005 and was honored as an NEA Jazz Master.

name: V. Globokar
bio: Slovenian-French composer, trombonist, and improviser. His works include Discours II for five trombones and draw on extended techniques, improvisation and music-theatre elements.

name: F. Tull
bio: American composer, arranger, and trumpeter with more than eighty published works, issued largely by Boosey & Hawkes.

name: R. Rudd
bio: American jazz trombonist and composer who began in Dixieland with Yale's Eli's Chosen Six. From 1962 he worked closely with Archie Shepp and recorded Thelonious Monk's music alongside soprano saxophonist Steve Lacy. In later years he made cross-cultural recordings with the Malian kora player Toumani Diabate and with the Mongolian Buryat Band.

name: S. Dempster
bio: American trombonist, didjeridu player and improviser who commissioned and performed works by composers including Berio, Ernst Krenek and Donald Erb; Berio's Sequenza V (1966) was written for him. He published The Modern Trombone: A Definition of Its Idioms (University of California Press, 1979).

name: B. Watrous
bio: American jazz trombonist renowned as a master technician with a mellifluous sound. He played and recorded with Count Basie, Woody Herman, and Quincy Jones, and taught at USC for two decades.

name: J. Eastman
bio: American composer, pianist, and vocalist whose post-minimalist works for multiple pianos explore his Black and gay identity.

name: D. Bourgeois
bio: English composer of 116 symphonies and extensive brass and wind band repertoire, including a Trombone Concerto (1988) and a Concerto for Bass Trombone and Band (2006). He served as director of the National Youth Orchestra (1984-1993) and director of music at St Paul's Girls' School (1994-2002).

name: F. Wesley
bio: American funk and jazz trombonist who served as band leader and musical director of James Brown's band, the J.B.'s, through the first half of the 1970s. After leaving in 1975 he performed with George Clinton's Parliament-Funkadelic, leading the spin-off Horny Horns, before joining the Count Basie Orchestra in 1978.

name: B. Slokar
bio: Slovenian-born trombonist and pedagogue who was a laureate at the Geneva International Competition in 1973 and a prizewinner at the ARD International Music Competition in Munich in 1974. He founded the Slokar Trombone Quartet and embraced a soloist career in 1979.

name: S. Turre
bio: American jazz trombonist known for pioneering the use of seashells as musical instruments alongside the trombone. He has been a member of the Saturday Night Live Band since 1985 and has performed across jazz, rock, and Latin jazz idioms.

name: C. Rouse
bio: American composer whose Trombone Concerto, written for Joseph Alessi and the New York Philharmonic, won the 1993 Pulitzer Prize for Music. He served as composer-in-residence for the New York Philharmonic from 2012 to 2015.

name: M. Becquet
bio: French trombonist who won all major international trombone competitions. He became solo trombone of the Orchestre de la Suisse Romande at age 18 and later became Head of Brass at the Conservatoire National Superieur de Musique de Lyon.

name: J. Sandström
bio: Swedish composer best known for his Motorbike Concerto for trombone and orchestra (1988-89), which has had over 600 performances. Written for Christian Lindberg, it is one of the most technically demanding trombone concertos ever composed.

name: E. Ewazen
bio: American composer on the faculty of The Juilliard School since 1980 who has written extensively for brass instruments. His compositions have been performed by numerous ensembles and orchestras around the world.

name: R. Eubanks
bio: American jazz trombonist who pioneered the use of electronic effects with the trombone and was one of the pioneers of the M-Base collective. He played for 15 years in Dave Holland's groups and served as professor at Oberlin Conservatory on J.J. Johnson's recommendation.

name: D. Yeo
bio: American bass trombonist who was in the Boston Symphony Orchestra from 1985 to 2012, holding the John Moors Cabot Bass Trombone Chair. He is also a scholar of historical brass instruments and has taught at Arizona State University, Wheaton College, and the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign.

name: N. Landgren
bio: Swedish jazz, funk, and R&B trombonist and singer known as The Man with the Red Horn for his trademark red trombone. By his own count he has contributed to at least 500 albums, including with ABBA and Herbie Hancock, and he received the Order of Merit of the Federal Republic of Germany in 2019.

name: C. Lindberg
bio: Swedish trombonist, conductor, and composer who was the first classical trombonist to sustain a full-time solo career. He has an extensive discography on BIS Records.

name: J. Alessi
bio: American trombonist who has served as Principal Trombone of the New York Philharmonic since 1985. He premiered Christopher Rouse's Pulitzer Prize-winning Trombone Concerto and teaches at The Juilliard School.

name: C. Herwig
bio: American jazz trombonist celebrated for his Afro-Caribbean and Latin jazz work. A frequent musical director of the Mingus Big Band and collaborator with Eddie Palmieri and Joe Lovano, he was repeatedly voted top trombonist in DownBeat's Critics' Poll and teaches jazz at Rutgers University.

name: I. Bousfield
bio: English trombonist who held the position of Principal Trombone with the Vienna Philharmonic, the London Symphony Orchestra, and the Halle Orchestra. He became the youngest winner of the LSO Music Scholarship in 1979.

name: A. Trudel
bio: Canadian conductor, trombonist, and composer from Montreal who made his solo debut at age 18 with Charles Dutoit and the Montreal Symphony Orchestra. He later became a conductor and was made a Knight of the National Order of Quebec in 2019.

name: W. Gordon
bio: American jazz trombonist, arranger and composer, many times named Jazz Trombonist of the Year by the Jazz Journalists Association. An original member of the Lincoln Center Jazz Orchestra (1995-2000), he also arranged the theme music for NPR's All Things Considered.

name: N. Haroz
bio: Israeli-born trombonist who is Principal Trombone of The Philadelphia Orchestra, a post he held from 1995 to 2012 and again since rejoining in 2014. He was Principal Trombone of the Los Angeles Philharmonic from 2012 to 2014 and has taught at the Curtis Institute of Music since 1998.

name: J. van Rijen
bio: Dutch trombonist who has been Principal Trombone of the Royal Concertgebouw Orchestra in Amsterdam since 1997. James MacMillan composed a trombone concerto for him, which he premiered in 2017, and he is an award-winning soloist (Netherlands Music Prize 2004, Borletti-Buitoni Trust Award 2006).

name: Trombone Shorty
bio: New Orleans musician whose music fuses rock, jazz, funk, and hip hop. He appeared at Jazz Fest at age four, was leading his own brass band by age six, and won his first Grammy in 2022.
